purpose: Road-layer specification extracted from one Simpsons Tapped Out-style town save (.pb). Reverse-engineered without a schema.

verified: wire layout of the layer wrapper
row-major block order at 37 blocks per row
cell byte alphabet and 4-bit neighbour mask with bit order E=1,W=2,N=4,S=8 (every set connection bit is reciprocated by its neighbour: 100.0% on this layer)
inferred: that layer type 2 is 'roads' (judged from shape only: long orthogonal runs, right-angle corners, T-junctions, rectangular loops, solid plazas)
1 cell = 4 world units, and layer origin = header origin (-3,-7) blocks x 16 = (-48,-112); object coordinates fit this range but alignment with roads was NOT confirmed
meaning of 'P' solid cells (plazas or paved areas?)
unknown: why the row width is 37 blocks: not stored in any field found; recovered by testing widths for neighbour consistency (only 37 gives 1.0)
what the layer type numbers are called in-game; only numbers are stored
whether per-tile road style/variant info exists elsewhere in the file (this layer has connectivity only)

layer_wrapper.4: varint layer type enum (2 for this layer)

related_header_field_4.2: 64*64 ASCII '0'/'1' land mask (40 columns of ones, 2366 ones; NOT the same footprint as the 37-wide layers)

container.length_note: data length 34784 = 2174 blocks x 16; 2174 = 58*37 + 28, so the last block row is partial

tile_layout.block_is: 4x4 cells, row-major (byte k -> cell row k//4, col k%4)
tile_layout.block_order: row-major, 37 blocks per row; block index b -> block col b%37, block row b//37
tile_layout.cell_row_col_from_offset: off=byte offset; b=off//16; k=off%16; col=(b%37)*4+(k%4); row=(b//37)*4+(k//4)

cell_byte_alphabet.P (0x50): solid filled cell, no connectivity bits; belongs to a shape only via adjacent P cells
cell_byte_alphabet.a..p (0x61..0x70): value=byte-0x61 is a neighbour mask; bit0=East, bit1=West, bit2=North, bit3=South; 'a'=isolated dot, 'p'=all four sides

tile_layout.reciprocity_rule: if a cell has bit E set, its east neighbour must have bit W set (likewise W/E and N/S). Holds for 100% of set bits in this layer; this is the main evidence the layout is right.
tile_layout.stride_note: a vertical road appears in the raw stream as the same byte every 4 bytes inside a block ('mGGGmGGGmGGGmGGG'), and the same block repeats every 37 blocks (592 bytes) down the map

road_data.grid_rows_note: 236 strings of 148 chars; 'G' empty. Row i, col j is cell (row i, col j) using the layout above.

raw_nonempty_blocks.note: block index -> the 16 bytes exactly as stored (ground truth). All other blocks are 16 x 'G'.
